sections.heading: Learning Point 4
sections.content: 28 Exploring Society: India and Beyond | Grade 7 Part 1 Weather and its Elements You wake up one winter morning and shiver.
sections.source_evidence: 28 Exploring Society: India and Beyond | Grade 7 Part 1 Weather and its Elements You wake up one winter morning and shiver.

sections.heading: Learning Point 5
sections.content: You reach for thick clothes to keep yourself warm.
sections.source_evidence: You reach for thick clothes to keep yourself warm.

sections.heading: Learning Point 6
sections.content: In the summer, you choose clothes that keep you cool and comfortable.

sections.heading: Learning Point 7
sections.content: You are responding to your body’s signals; your body is sensing the weather.

sections.heading: Learning Point 8
sections.content: Weather is a state of the Earth’s atmosphere at a particular time and place.
sections.source_evidence: Weather is a state of the Earth’s atmosphere at a particular time and place.

sections.heading: Learning Point 9
sections.content: In simple terms, it is the layer of gases that surround some planets — in the case of our Earth, we call these gases ‘air’.
sections.source_evidence: In simple terms, it is the layer of gases that surround some planets — in the case of our Earth, we call these gases ‘air’.

sections.heading: Learning Point 10
sections.content: The Earth’s atmosphere may be compared to a cake with several layers.
sections.source_evidence: The Earth’s atmosphere may be compared to a cake with several layers.

sections.heading: Learning Point 11
sections.content: The layer closest to the surface of the Earth is called the ‘troposphere’, and that is where all land-based plants and animals (including humans!) live and breathe.
sections.source_evidence: The layer closest to the surface of the Earth is called the ‘troposphere’, and that is where all land-based plants and animals (including humans!) live and breathe.

sections.heading: Learning Point 12
sections.content: It is also where almost all weather phenomena, which we will explore in this chapter, take place.
sections.source_evidence: It is also where almost all weather phenomena, which we will explore in this chapter, take place.

sections.heading: Learning Point 13
sections.content: The troposphere extends to a height of 6 to 18 kilometres from the ground; it is less thick at the poles (where the cold air contracts) and thicker in the tropical zone (where the warmer air expands).
sections.source_evidence: The troposphere extends to a height of 6 to 18 kilometres from the ground; it is less thick at the poles (where the cold air contracts) and thicker in the tropical zone (where the warmer air expands).

sections.heading: Learning Point 14
sections.content: You will study more about the other layers in your Science classes.

sections.heading: Learning Point 15
sections.content: We use many words to describe the weather — hot, cold, rainy, cloudy, humid, snowy, windy, and so on.
sections.source_evidence: We use many words to describe the weather — hot, cold, rainy, cloudy, humid, snowy, windy, and so on.

sections.heading: Learning Point 16
sections.content: They describe the different ways in which we experience the elements of weather.

sections.heading: Learning Point 20
sections.content: 29 India and the World: Land and the People 2 – Understanding the Weather The elements of weather are:  Temperature: How hot or cold the atmosphere is.  Precipitation: Any form of water, such as rain, snow, sleet or hail, that falls from the sky.  Atmospheric Pressure: The weight of the air above us, felt on the Earth’s surface.  Wind: The movement of air, including its speed and direction.  Humidity: The amount of water vapour in the air.
